newsitem.title: MEXICO: GFINBURSA HEAD CHICO PARDO QUITS.
newsitem.headline: GFINBURSA HEAD CHICO PARDO QUITS.

text.p: Fernando Chico Pardo has announced his resignation as director general of Grupo Financiero Inbursa and as chief executive of Banco Inbursa, but will remain on the board, sources said on Tuesday.
"Fernando wanted to set up his own business," a senior source at the bank told Reuters. "He has quit as director general on the best of terms."
The source said Carlos Slim, chief executive of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, would temporarily take Chico Pardo's place as chief executive of Banco Inbursa while a replacement was sought.

The replacement would "without a doubt come from within the group," the source said. He said there was no hurry for Chico Pardo to leave and that he may remain at his post for another two or three months.

Inbursa is Mexico's most profitable banking group and under Chico Pardo has eschewed retail banking to concentrate on lending to top-tier corporations. It is also considered a savvy player in Mexican financial markets, has a profitable insurance arm, Seguros Inbursa, and a strong mutual funds business.
It reported a net profit of 2.404 billion pesos in the first six months of 1997.
